questions.prompt: Why does the announcement want schools to go beyond keeping phones quiet?
options: Keeping phones quiet also keeps them beyond pupils’ reach.
Phones can remain accessible under the existing rule.
The existing rule already prevents access throughout the day.
Keeping phones in bags already removes pressure to go online.
questions.explanationZh: 现有“不被看见、不发声”规定仍可能让手机留在书包里；新指导希望进一步限制取用，而非文中其他原因。

questions.prompt: Which approach is described as already being used by some schools?
options: Collecting phones after lessons rather than before the day.
Keeping phones locked away during lessons but not breaks.
Collecting devices when the school day begins.
Using safety certificates instead of rules about phone access.
questions.explanationZh: 第6句明确列出上学时收走手机；其他做法未被描述为已有实践。

questions.prompt: How do the phone guidance and technology consultation differ?
options: One restricts personal phone access; the other explores safety standards for learning technology.
One tests personal phone safety; the other explores storage rules for classroom devices.
One restricts phones during lessons; the other extends those restrictions to school breaks.
One certifies learning technology now; the other checks whether phone restrictions have succeeded.
questions.explanationZh: 第4句谈全天限制个人手机取用，第11至13句另谈学习技术的安全与可能认证；并不是给手机做安全检测、把课堂禁令延长至课间，或已完成认证和成效评估。

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the status of these measures?
options: They report improvements measured in every English school.
They replace all existing school rules with one storage method.
They confirm that classroom technology has passed new tests.
They set directions for phone restrictions and explore technology safeguards.
questions.explanationZh: 本文报告指导计划及意见征集，不是全校成效评估、单一保管方式或已完成的技术认证。
